bug_semantics: Before 0.12.0, c3p0 represented the writable JavaBean property userOverridesAsString as 'HexAsciiSerializedMap[' plus hex-encoded Java serialization bytes. C3P0ImplUtils.parseUserOverridesAsString() stripped that wrapper, hex-decoded attacker-controlled bytes, and passed them to SerializableUtils.fromByteArray() without an allowlist. WrapperConnectionPoolDataSource invoked this parser from its vetoable-change listener whenever the property was reset, and ComboPooledDataSource exported the property through its javax.naming.Reference. An attacker able to supply a crafted property value directly, through a serialized ConnectionPoolDataSource, or through a JNDI Reference could therefore trigger gadget deserialization. In combination with the dependency's then-ungated indirect JNDI Reference/factoryClassLocation handling, this could download and execute attacker code; independently, deserializing arbitrary objects from a writable bean string was unsafe.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable mechanism first appears in the preserved public tree at e11fd1340644747977fa34bc3377704223b6ccb4, the c3p0-0.9.1-pre5 source-release snapshot import. That snapshot added C3P0ImplUtils.createUserOverridesAsString()/parseUserOverridesAsString(), the WrapperConnectionPoolDataSource listener that calls the parser, the constrained generated property, and ComboPooledDataSource's Reference exposure. Its parent 15b53cfce6ed1fb0a46fd6597c2b2e4470e6f8c9 (c3p0-0.9.0.4) has none of those identifiers. However, e11fd1340644747977fa34bc3377704223b6ccb4 is a 270-file import of a SourceForge release ZIP rather than the atomic changeset that authored the flawed mechanism, so the protocol forbids treating it as the BIC.
ai_marker: unavailable: the smallest BIC commit object is not present in the public history, so no BIC-only author, committer, or trailer AI assessment can be made; the release-snapshot import is not used as an attribution substitute
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/swaldman/c3p0/security/advisories/GHSA-5476-xc4j-rqcv identifies affected com.mchange:c3p0 versions < 0.12.0, patched versions 0.12.0+, and the direct patch https://github.com/swaldman/c3p0/commit/e14cbd8166e423e2e9a9d6f08b2add3433492d6e. It describes malicious serialized ConnectionPoolDataSources and javax.naming.Reference instances, writable userOverridesAsString, hex-encoded Java serialization, and the mchange-commons-java remote factoryClassLocation amplification.

At e11fd1340644747977fa34bc3377704223b6ccb4, src/classes/com/mchange/v2/c3p0/impl/C3P0ImplUtils.java:172-194 defines HASM_HEADER='HexAsciiSerializedMap'; createUserOverridesAsString() calls SerializableUtils.toByteArray(), and parseUserOverridesAsString() calls ByteUtils.fromHexAscii() followed by SerializableUtils.fromByteArray().

At the same tree, src/classes/com/mchange/v2/c3p0/WrapperConnectionPoolDataSource.java:72-78 handles a userOverridesAsString property change by calling C3P0ImplUtils.parseUserOverridesAsString(); lines 89-92 also parse the initial value. src/classes/com/mchange/v2/c3p0/ComboPooledDataSource.java:475-481 forwards the public setter, and lines 533-556 include userOverridesAsString among JavaBeanReferenceMaker properties. src/codegen/com/mchange/v2/c3p0/impl/WrapperConnectionPoolDataSourceBase.beangen-xml:184-193 declares it as a constrained String property.

History search with `git log --all --reverse -S'HexAsciiSerializedMap' -- .`, `git log --all --reverse -S'userOverridesAsString' -- .`, and full-history path tracing found the first preserved vulnerable source only in e11fd1340644747977fa34bc3377704223b6ccb4. Later 7ff5d91ae823c8fb9dcdd3f040d274a94bcf4aa6 is another initial GitHub snapshot and 36182b4a5fd024703e2a36737b2b73ad7237f1f8 is a move/reorganization, so neither is a smallest origin.

`git show --format=fuller --stat e11fd1340644747977fa34bc3377704223b6ccb4` identifies the candidate as 'source imported from SourceForge (c3p0-0.9.1-pre5.src.zip)', with parent 15b53cfce6ed1fb0a46fd6597c2b2e4470e6f8c9 and 270 changed files. This is a release-snapshot aggregate, not an atomic authoring commit, and no member SHAs exist in the validated clone to decompose it.

Direct parent-tree verification used `git grep -n -E 'HexAsciiSerializedMap|parseUserOverridesAsString|userOverridesAsString' 15b53cfce6ed1fb0a46fd6597c2b2e4470e6f8c9 -- src/classes/com/mchange/v2/c3p0` and returned no matches. Running the corresponding grep at e11fd1340644747977fa34bc3377704223b6ccb4 returned the parser in C3P0ImplUtils.java and its callers in WrapperConnectionPoolDataSource.java and C3P0PooledConnectionPoolManager.java. This proves absence from the snapshot import's immediate parent, but not absence from the unavailable true BIC parent.

Version membership is exact: `git rev-parse c3p0-0.9.0.4^{}` = 15b53cfce6ed1fb0a46fd6597c2b2e4470e6f8c9; `git rev-parse c3p0-0.9.1-pre5^{}` = e11fd1340644747977fa34bc3377704223b6ccb4. Thus the unsafe property was absent from 0.9.0.4 and present in 0.9.1-pre5. `git rev-parse v0.12.0^{}` = afbb946ea70ee2312c1c5fc53dd60dd218f87ef9, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor e14cbd8166e423e2e9a9d6f08b2add3433492d6e v0.12.0^{}` succeeded, placing the fix before the patched tag.

Patch e14cbd8166e423e2e9a9d6f08b2add3433492d6e directly disables the Java-serialization implementation in src/com/mchange/v2/c3p0/impl/C3P0ImplUtils.java and replaces it with ragged-CSV generation/parsing through FastCsvUtils; this removes the attacker-controlled ObjectInputStream path. Therefore both fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are this advisory-linked commit.

The missing atomic SourceForge history is a genuine public-history boundary: the validated clone preserves only release-ZIP import commits for this era, the former c3p0 SourceForge CVS page no longer exposes a repository, and the standard SourceForge CVS snapshot URL https://sourceforge.net/code-snapshots/cvs/c/c3/c3p0.zip returned HTTP 404 on 2026-08-28.
reasoning: The vulnerability is the active conversion of a writable, externally reconstructable bean property into unrestricted Java object deserialization. The property setter and initialization paths call the unsafe parser, while Reference serialization exposes the property across JNDI; a gadget in the application classpath is sufficient for unexpected execution, and the historical dependency's indirect Reference/factoryClassLocation support made remote code loading practical. The advisory's fix rewrites the representation as CSV and is an ancestor of the 0.12.0 patched tag. History establishes a sharp preserved-tree boundary between c3p0-0.9.0.4 and c3p0-0.9.1-pre5, and direct comparison proves the complete mechanism absent from the former and present in the latter. But the latter SHA is explicitly a broad SourceForge release-ZIP snapshot import, not the smallest authoring changeset. Because the protocol disallows using squash/import aggregates as BICs and the original CVS atomic revision and its parent are not recoverable from the validated clone or the retired public CVS archive, introducer_sha and introducer_parent must remain null, introducer_parent_absent must remain false for the unknown real parent, and AI attribution cannot be assessed from any substitute commit. This is BLOCKED rather than EVIDENCE_GAP because the named missing evidence lies beyond a retired public-history boundary, not merely an uncompleted reachable search.
remaining_gap: Recover the original atomic SourceForge CVS changeset that first added the HexAsciiSerializedMap Java-deserialization parser together with the writable/listener/Reference exposure, plus that changeset's immediate parent, then verify parent absence and inspect that changeset's commit object for AI signals. The current repository only has the non-decomposable c3p0-0.9.1-pre5 release-snapshot import e11fd1340644747977fa34bc3377704223b6ccb4, and SourceForge's c3p0 CVS snapshot is unavailable (HTTP 404).
